newsitem.title: GERMANY: Chirpy Bunds on track for more gains.
newsitem.headline: Chirpy Bunds on track for more gains.

text.p: The German Bund market received a welcome dose of medicine in late Tuesday trade as U.S. credit markets reacted positively to benign confidence and inflation indicators.
But despite a healthy leg up in price levels, Bunds lagged behind the U.S. market on spread performance, narrowing the 10-year gap to 107 basis points from 117 in early trade.
Dealers said the underperformance was nothing to be concerned about, and served only to show the extent of relief in the U.S. market that the data were friendly.
"The only influence on the Bunds at the moment is the U.S. market," said one Frankfurt-based broker.
"The figures today lent some good support, and the Bund market has rallied with good volumes. It looks pretty sturdy."
By 1423 GMT, the June DTB Bund future was trading 50 basis points higher on the day at 100.92, off its earlier peak at 101.04 but well above the low of 100.45.

The markets were pleased by U.S. data showing the April consumer confidence index slipping to 116.8 from 11.5 in March, and first quarter 1997 employment costs up 0.6 percent versus a 0.8 percent gain in the fourth quarter 1996.
Analysts said that with this session's rally supported by decent volume, the German market should continue to head higher in the coming sessions.

"Although the rally today was sparked by the States, the German economic factors are also very supportive for Bunds," said a trader in Frankfurt. "The German market has much more there in terms of support than the U.S. has."
In the cash market, the 10-year Bund due January 2007 was trading at 101.19 by 1430 GMT for a yield of 5.825 percent, while three-year paper was quoted at 100.26 for 3.597 percent yield.
